fatal_errors: The proposed ammonia nitridation intervention is unrelated to the target closed-loop high-throughput synthesis, ageing-screening, machine-learning, and Bayesian-optimisation campaign.

The asserted nitrogen-stabilized Pt-enriched shell, Pt leaching, and metal–nitrogen mechanism have no supplied supporting evidence and do not match the observed Cu–Pt electronic reconstruction and process-dependent alloy/support states.

The hypothesis assumes that the untreated catalyst had already demonstrated deactivation, whereas the target starting materials were fresh candidates and ageing could either improve or impair activity.
It omits the defined Pd/Al2O3 and random-exploration baselines and the quantitative post-ageing performance criteria.
The exhaust composition, severe 900 °C cyclic lean/rich water-containing ageing protocol, and species-resolved conversion endpoints are not specified.
explanation: The response addresses the broad goal of improving low-PGM catalyst durability under water-containing, low-temperature automotive exhaust, but it does not reconstruct the target intervention or its central finding that severe ageing can beneficially reconstruct multimetal sites. Its proposed nitrogen doping and protective Pt shell are speculative because no prior evidence is cited, and neither Pt leaching nor nitridation is established as relevant to the target system. The matched treated-versus-untreated ageing test is a reasonable preliminary experiment, but it lacks the target feed, Pd benchmark, species-resolved NO/CO/hydrocarbon metrics, and direct tests capable of distinguishing M–N stabilization from other treatment effects. XPS and TEM alone would not decisively establish a Pt-enriched shell or its causal role.
